guests.name: Bartholomew
guests.bio: Bellhop since 1923. Knows every room, every guest and every creak.
guests.arrival: Bartholomew[happy]: First guest of the night: me! Put me next to somebody. I do love a chat.

guests.name: Captain Morrow
guests.bio: Still waiting for a ship that never came back.
guests.arrival:
Captain Morrow: Captain Elias Morrow, of the Lark.
A room with water, if you please. And no attics. Too far from the sea.
story: Captain Morrow[sad]: Every night I watch the lake. The Lark should have been home by now.
Captain Morrow: There's a lantern on the far shore some nights. Could be her. Could be anyone.
Captain Morrow: I found my logbook in the lake-view room. The last page... I never read it.

Captain Morrow[happy]: "All hands safe ashore." They made it. They made it home.
I think I can stop waiting now.
guests.checkout: Captain Morrow[happy]: Take my compass, keeper. It always points to what's hidden.

guests.name: Lady Ashworth
guests.bio: Insists on the finest room, a mirror to check her hat, and no riff-raff next door.
guests.arrival:
Lady Ashworth: A room with a mirror. The highest you have.
And keep that dreadful poltergeist away from my wall.
story: Lady Ashworth: Hmph. Adequate. My portrait used to hang in this very hall, you know.
Lady Ashworth[sad]: The mirror shows a hat I was buried in. I never liked that hat.
Lady Ashworth[happy]: I've decided I quite like it after all. How freeing, to be wrong.
guests.checkout: Lady Ashworth[happy]: Keep my hatpin. Ladies must look after one another.

guests.name: Pip
guests.bio: Scared of the dark, never scared of company.
guests.arrival:
Pip[happy]: Hi! I'm Pip! Can I have a room that isn't dark? And next to somebody?
Not the crying lady though. She makes me sad.
story: Pip: I'm looking for my kite. It got stuck in a tree by the lake. A long time ago.
Pip[sad]: I asked the crying lady if she'd seen it. She just cried more. Sorry, Gloria.
Pip[happy]: The groundskeeper says there's a red kite in the big pine! It has to be mine!
Pip[happy]: It IS mine! Mum sewed my name on the tail. I can go home now, can't I?
guests.checkout: Pip[happy]: You can have my marble. It's the shiny one. Bye!

guests.name: Gloria
guests.bio: Cries quietly. Please don't make her cry loudly.
guests.arrival:
Gloria[sad]: A dark room, please. Somewhere quiet.
And... I can't bear to see my own face.
story: Gloria[sad]: I sang here once. The night of the big storm. I never finished the song.
Gloria: The old piano in the ballroom still has my sheet music on it. Fancy that.
Gloria[happy]: I finished it tonight. Nobody heard but me, and that was enough.
guests.checkout: Gloria[happy]: Here, my sheet music. Hum it sometime.

guests.name: Rattles
guests.bio: Loud, chaotic and secretly lonely. Lives for a good attic.
guests.arrival:
Rattles[happy]: RATTLES IS HERE! Attic room, obviously. Nobody else gets the good rafters.
Mirrors give me the creeps. And it's quiet up there. Too quiet. Someone come visit?
story: Rattles: Nobody ever wants to be my neighbour. It's the chains. People hate the chains.
Rattles[happy]: Turns out the chains were from a swing set! I was just... swinging. For forty years.
guests.checkout: Rattles[happy]: Keep the chain! Swing responsibly!

guests.name: Wren
guests.bio: A tiny shy light. Brightens any room next to it, whether you like it or not.
guests.arrival:
Wren[sad]: ...hello. I'm small. I'll be no trouble. Somewhere alone, or high up, near the sky.
I just glow a little. The dark rooms next to me stop being dark. Sorry.
story: Wren: I don't remember being anything but a light. Is that strange?
Wren[sad]: A little girl followed me through the marsh once. I was trying to lead her home. She thought I was leading her away.
Wren: Ivy says I'm the nicest light she's ever met. I didn't know lights could be nice.
Wren[happy]: I remember now. I was a lantern in a window, waiting for someone to come home. They came home. I can go out now.
guests.checkout: Wren[happy]: Keep my wick. It still smells of warm wax.

guests.name: Sir Aldric
guests.bio: Guards the cellar. Can't abide mirrors, which only show what's missing.
guests.arrival:
Sir Aldric: (His helmet speaks from under his arm.) Sir Aldric. I keep the lower halls.
A cellar room. Some company. And no mirrors. I know full well what is missing.
story: Sir Aldric: I lost my head over a wager. Literally. The other knight never paid up.
Sir Aldric[sad]: Tobias says a dog scratches at the cellar door. I have been guarding a dog. For six hundred years.
Sir Aldric[happy]: The dog and I have made our peace. A knight may rest when his post is relieved.
guests.checkout: Sir Aldric[happy]: My spur, keeper. You have earned it, defending this house.

guests.name: Moira
guests.bio: Her screech goes straight through floors and ceilings.
guests.arrival:
Moira: I keen, keeper. It's what I am. It goes up and down through the floors, never sideways.
A corner room. And keep the little ones away. I frighten them.
story: Moira[sad]: I keened for every death in the village for two hundred years. Nobody ever keened for me.
Moira: The singer, Marisol, says my voice has a lovely range. Nobody has ever said lovely about my voice.
Moira[sad]: Vane wants to bottle my voice. He says it would sell. I said no. He smiled anyway.
Moira[happy]: Marisol keened for me tonight. Badly. Beautifully. I can stop now.
guests.checkout: Moira[happy]: My comb. Silver, for a banshee's hair. Brush gently.

guests.name: Tobias
guests.bio: Pip's best friend from the old street. Terrified of the cellar.
guests.arrival:
Tobias[sad]: Is Pip here? Pip said this was a nice hotel.
Not the dark rooms. And NOT the cellar. Something scratches down there.
story: Tobias[sad]: I followed Pip into the lake that day. I was only trying to help with the kite.
Tobias: The scratching in the cellar is a dog. MY dog. Biscuit waited for me all this time.
Tobias[happy]: Biscuit remembered me! We're going to find Pip together.
guests.checkout: Tobias[happy]: Here's Biscuit's old collar. He says thanks for the room.

guests.name: Elsie
guests.bio: A war widow who still sets the table for two. Wants to be closer to the stars.
guests.arrival:
Elsie[sad]: A dark room near the roof, please. I like to be nearer the stars.
And somewhere quiet. Children's laughter is... difficult.
story: Elsie[sad]: Arthur went to the front in 1916. I set his place every evening. I still do.
Elsie: The attic window faces east. Arthur's letters always came from the east.
Elsie[happy]: I found his last letter tucked in the lining of my coat. "Don't wait up, love. I'll find you." So I'll go and be found.
guests.checkout: Elsie[happy]: Keep his letter safe for me. I won't need it where I'm going.

guests.name: Finn
guests.bio: Cabin boy of the Lark. Prefers the ground floor, near the water, away from fancy folk.
guests.arrival:
Finn: Finn, cabin boy of the Lark, at your service! A room with water, if it's no trouble.
Ground floor's best. And no posh types next door. They look at me funny.
story: Finn[sad]: The Captain stayed with the ship. I couldn't swim back to him. I've felt rotten ever since.
Finn[happy]: Captain Morrow's logbook says I was the bravest on board. ME! Imagine that.
guests.checkout: Finn[happy]: Have my bosun's whistle. Blow it and I'll hear you, wherever I am.

guests.name: Cornelia
guests.bio: Lady Ashworth's rival. Insists on a mirror, a fire, and no poltergeists.
guests.arrival:
Cornelia: Cornelia Vane-Hartley. I require a mirror. A fire would be civilised.
And keep those rattling things away. I will not share a wall with a poltergeist.
story: Cornelia: Lady Ashworth stole my seat at the Winter Ball of 1881. I have not forgotten.
Cornelia[sad]: I found her old dance card. She wrote my name on it, then crossed it out. Why?
Cornelia[happy]: She meant to ask ME to dance, the silly thing, and lost her nerve. A hundred and forty years of sulking, wasted.
guests.checkout: Cornelia[happy]: Take the dance card. And if you see Ashworth, tell her... the next waltz is hers.

guests.name: Ned
guests.bio: Smashes plates when bored. Water rusts his chains and gloom gives him the creeps.
guests.arrival:
Ned[happy]: Ned! Hi! Don't put me near water, my chains go all crunchy.
Neighbours are great. Just not the weepy ones. Bit of a downer, no offence.
story: Ned[sad]: I broke all of Mum's good plates the night I... you know. Never said sorry.
Ned[happy]: There's a stack of plates in the hotel kitchen with Mum's pattern. I glued one back together. It's a start.
guests.checkout: Ned[happy]: Here, a bit of the plate I fixed. Mostly glue, honestly.

guests.name: Old Bramble
guests.bio: Wants the ground floor, the far end, and no fuss.
guests.arrival: Old Bramble: Ground floor. End room. No fuss. No neighbours. That's all.
story: Old Bramble: Built this place, I did. The foundations. Dug deeper than they told me to. Should've stopped.
Old Bramble[happy]: Told Greaves where the old door is. Bricked it up myself, 1648. Whatever's behind it, it's been waiting a long time. Not my problem now.
guests.checkout: Old Bramble: My trowel. You'll be needing it.

guests.name: Ivy
guests.bio: Lost in the marsh as a girl. Follows lights. Wants to be next to Wren.
guests.arrival:
Ivy[happy]: Is the little light here? The one called Wren? I want the room right next to it!
No dark rooms please. And no screamy ladies.
story: Ivy[sad]: I followed a light into the marsh and never came out. I wasn't scared, though. It was pretty.
Ivy: Wren says it was trying to lead me home. I believe it. Lights don't lie.
Ivy[happy]: Wren told me where home was. It's not far. I'm going to walk there now, slowly, and look at everything.
guests.checkout: Ivy[happy]: Here's my ribbon. Tie it on a lantern so people find their way.

guests.name: Hester
guests.bio: A governess who covered every mirror in the house. Won't say why.
guests.hiddenHint: I can't bear to see my own face...
guests.arrival:
Hester[sad]: A dark room, high up. Thank you.
And... no. Never mind. I'm sure it will be fine.
story: Hester[sad]: I was a governess here, when it was a house. The children were dears. The mirrors were not.
Hester: Something lived in the mirrors. It wore my face and smiled when I didn't. I covered every one.
Hester[sad]: Mr. Vane asked me about the mirrors yesterday. Very politely. Too politely.
Hester[happy]: The thing in the mirror was only ever me, afraid. I looked at it tonight. It looked back, and it was tired too. We're both going to rest.
guests.checkout: Hester[happy]: My hand mirror. You can uncover it now.

guests.name: Mags
guests.bio: Throws teacups when she's nervous, which is always. Hates mirrors and misery.
guests.arrival:
Mags[happy]: Mags! Sorry about the noise, it just happens. No mirrors, please, I throw things at them.
Neighbours are lovely! Not the weepy kind though. I can't stand it when people cry, I start throwing teacups.
story: Mags: I ran the tea room downstairs in the sixties. Best scones in the county. Then the fire.
Mags[sad]: I keep throwing teacups because my hands remember the fire. They want to throw water on it.
Mags: Old Salt taught me to breathe like the tide. In for six, out for six. Only broke two cups today.
Mags[happy]: I made scones tonight. Real ones, in the old oven. Nobody threw anything. I'm done.
guests.checkout: Mags[happy]: The last teacup! Unbroken. A miracle.

guests.name: Lord Fenwick
guests.bio: A ruined lord who still dresses for dinner. Wants solitude, and a mirror for his cravat.
guests.hiddenHint: Damp ruins a good waistcoat. Not that one would complain.
guests.arrival:
Lord Fenwick: Fenwick. Lord. A mirror for my cravat, and no neighbours, if it can be managed.
The rest is of no consequence. One does not complain.
story: Lord Fenwick: I gambled the family estate away in a single night. To a polite man in a top hat.
Lord Fenwick[sad]: The man was Vane. He has been collecting deeds for a very long time, it seems.
Lord Fenwick: I have written to my great-granddaughter. She runs a bakery. She is happy. The estate would only have been a burden.
Lord Fenwick[happy]: I have nothing left to lose, which turns out to be a remarkable thing to have. Goodnight, keeper.
guests.checkout: Lord Fenwick[happy]: My signet ring. Never wager it.

guests.name: Old Salt
guests.bio: A lighthouse keeper. Wants water, the ground floor, and no singing.
guests.hiddenHint: Sirens. Never sleep near a singer.
guests.arrival:
Old Salt: Kept the Hollow Point light forty years. Water, ground floor, nothing fancy.
And... ah, never mind. An old sailor's superstition.
story: Old Salt: The night the light went out, a ship hit the rocks. I was asleep. I've been awake ever since.
Old Salt[sad]: Captain Morrow's Lark. It was the Lark, keeper. I've been afraid to ask if he forgave me.
Old Salt[happy]: Morrow left a note in his logbook for me. 'The fog was too thick for any light.' Forty years, and it wasn't my fault.
guests.checkout: Old Salt[happy]: The lighthouse key. Leave a light on for someone.

guests.name: Lumen
guests.bio: A brighter, braver wisp. Likes corners and the sky. Dislikes rattling.
guests.hiddenHint: It's so far from the sky down there...
guests.arrival:
Lumen[happy]: Another light! Hello! A corner room, so I can see out two windows.
No rattling neighbours. And, um... I'd rather be nearer the sky.
story: Lumen: Wren is my sister, I think. We came from the same window.
Lumen[sad]: The cellar frightens me. Something down there eats light. I felt it reach for me.
Lumen[happy]: I lit the cellar stairs for Sir Greaves tonight and nothing ate me. I'm braver than I was. That's enough.
guests.checkout: Lumen[happy]: A spark for your pocket. It won't burn.

guests.name: Sir Greaves
guests.bio: Guards the cellar door. Wishes to serve a proper noble, upstairs or adjacent.
guests.arrival:
Sir Greaves: (The helmet clanks.) Greaves. I guard doors. The cellar door, by preference.
A noble neighbour would be fitting. And no mirrors.
story: Sir Greaves: Sir Aldric was my master. He never told me he had moved on. I have been guarding his door all this time.
Sir Greaves[sad]: There is a door under the cellar, keeper. It was not there before. I hear Edith's voice behind it.
Sir Greaves: Vane offered me a new master. I said a knight chooses his own. He did not like that.
Sir Greaves[happy]: I have chosen. I serve this hotel, and its keeper, and I will hold that door until you are ready. Then I rest.
guests.checkout: Sir Greaves[happy]: My gauntlet. Throw it down when you need a champion.

guests.name: Marisol
guests.bio: A wartime singer. Needs music, and an audience.
guests.arrival:
Marisol[happy]: Darling! Marisol, the Nightingale of the Blitz. A room with a gramophone, or I simply won't sing.
And neighbours, please. A singer needs an audience. Even if they cover their ears.
story: Marisol: I sang in the shelters while the bombs fell. Kept everyone calm. Nobody kept me calm.
Marisol[sad]: My voice went strange after. High. Terrible. People said I'd become a banshee. They weren't wrong.
Marisol[happy]: Moira and I are rehearsing. Two banshees in harmony. Bartholomew wept. Possibly from joy.
Marisol[happy]: We sang for Moira tonight. She's free. And so, I think, am I. Encore? No. Curtain.
guests.checkout: Marisol[happy]: My gramophone needle. Play something sad and lovely.

guests.name: Mr. Thorne
guests.bio: The old head gardener. Needs the greenhouse and peace, and loathes poltergeists.
guests.arrival:
Mr. Thorne: Thorne. Head gardener, once. A room by the greenhouse.
Quiet. No poltergeists. They knock over the pots.
story: Mr. Thorne: Edith and I planted every rose on the north wall. She talked to them. I pretended not to.
Mr. Thorne[sad]: The roses are dying from the roots up. Something is poisoning the soil under the hotel.
Mr. Thorne[happy]: I grafted a cutting from Edith's rose. It'll outlive the rot. Plant it somewhere you'll see it.
guests.checkout: Mr. Thorne[happy]: A rose cutting. Water it on Sundays.

guests.name: Dolly
guests.bio: Bartholomew's little sister. Wants to be next to him. Frightened of knights.
guests.arrival:
Dolly[happy]: Barty! It's me, Dolly! Can I have the room next to my big brother?
Not the dark ones. And the clanky men with no heads are scary.
story: Dolly: Barty worked here as a bellboy so we'd have money. I used to wait for him by the back door.
Dolly[sad]: There was a fever that winter. I didn't wake up. Barty stayed here instead of going home. Because home was too sad.
Dolly[happy]: Barty says he'll stay and help the keeper, but I should go on ahead and save him a seat. I will! The best seat.
guests.checkout: Dolly[happy]: My spinning top. Give it to Barty when he's ready to come.

guests.name: The Stranger
guests.bio: A veiled guest who gives only riddles.
riddleClues: "I drowned once. Never again will I sleep where water lies."
"I came here to be alone. A neighbour on any side would spoil it."
"Rattling chains remind me of the ship. Keep them far from me."
guests.arrival:
The Stranger: (A veiled figure. Its voice is familiar, but you can't place it.)
I won't tell you what I need. Listen to what I say instead.
story: The Stranger: You placed me well. Edith would have, too. Did you know she kept every guest's needs in her head?
The Stranger[happy]: (The veil slips. It's a younger Edith, or the memory of her.) Not yet, love. Keep going. You're nearly ready to find me.
guests.checkout: The Stranger[happy]: My veil. Next time, you'll see my face.

guests.name: Rowena
guests.bio: Lost her husband to one of Vane's deals. Wants a quiet room under someone respectable.
guests.hiddenHint: Crowded corridors make me feel I can't breathe...
guests.arrival:
Rowena[sad]: A dark room, low down. Or beneath a respectable gentleman, if you have one. They used to keep the noise off.
I shan't trouble you with the rest.
story: Rowena[sad]: My Henry signed a paper for a man in a top hat. Then Henry was gone, and so was the house.
Rowena: Lord Fenwick says Vane collects the people with the deeds. Henry is in his warehouse somewhere. Waiting.
Rowena[happy]: Edith found Henry. She sent him out the other side. He's waiting for me there, she says. I'm going.
guests.checkout: Rowena[happy]: Henry's pocket watch. It stopped the day he signed. It's ticking again.

guests.name: Mr. Barnaby
guests.bio: Vane's former bookkeeper. Wants a mirror, a quiet floor, and no banshees.
guests.arrival:
Mr. Barnaby: Barnaby. Formerly of Vane and Associates. A mirror, if you please, and a floor that isn't crowded.
No banshees. I've heard enough screaming in my career.
story: Mr. Barnaby[sad]: I kept Vane's books for forty years. Every soul he bought, I wrote down. In ink.
Mr. Barnaby: I still have the ledger, keeper. Every name. If you could free them, I could cross them out.
Mr. Barnaby[happy]: Seventeen names crossed out tonight. The ink is fading. So, pleasantly, am I.
guests.checkout: Mr. Barnaby[happy]: Vane's old ledger. Burn it when the last name is gone.

guests.name: Sir Corvin
guests.bio: The oldest knight in the cellar. Serves beneath nobles, literally.
guests.arrival:
Sir Corvin: (A rusted helmet, very old.) Corvin. I guard from below. Put a noble above me, and I'll keep them safe.
No mirrors. You know why.
story: Sir Corvin: Greaves and Aldric were my squires, once. Good lads. They kept the cellar door while I slept.
Sir Corvin[sad]: The door is open a crack now. I've seen what's behind it. Shelves. Thousands of shelves. Jars with lights in them.
Sir Corvin[happy]: Every light that leaves a jar goes home. I've seen it. That's worth guarding for. Now I'll rest, and you'll guard.
guests.checkout: Sir Corvin[happy]: My broken sword. The other half is in the in-between. Bring it back.

guests.name: Cobb
guests.bio: A chimney sweep who thinks the curse is cosy. Likes crowds, up to a point.
guests.arrival:
Cobb[happy]: Cobb, sweep! Curse in the room? Lovely, feels like a warm chimney.
Put me with folk. Not too many, mind, I get rattly.
story: Cobb: I got stuck up the hotel chimney in '38. Nobody heard me knocking. Funny, cos I'm loud now.
Cobb[sad]: The curse is warm because it's hungry, keeper. It's trying to swallow the rooms. I'll keep it busy.
Cobb[happy]: Found the way out of the chimney. It goes up! Always did. Cheerio.
guests.checkout: Cobb[happy]: My brush. Sweep the curse out, it's only soot really.

guests.name: Nell
guests.bio: The lake ferry woman. Likes to sleep above another sailor, or right by the water.
guests.arrival:
Nell: Nell, ferry woman. Water, please. Ground floor, or above another sailor, I'm not fussy.
No poltergeists. They rock the boat.
story: Nell: I rowed the dead across the lake for sixty years. Then one night I rowed myself.
Nell[sad]: Young Tam drowned on my last crossing. I couldn't reach him. I've been rowing in circles looking.
Nell[happy]: Tam's found. He was waiting on the far shore, the silly boy. We'll cross together.
guests.checkout: Nell[happy]: My oarlock. Keep someone afloat.

guests.name: Tam
guests.bio: A boy who fell off Nell's ferry. Wants to be next to Nell.
guests.hiddenHint: It was so cold in the water... I don't ever want to be cold again.
guests.arrival:
Tam[sad]: Is Nell here? The ferry lady? I want to be near her. And near water. I like water. I'm not scared of it.
I'm just... a bit cold.
story: Tam[sad]: I fell off the ferry reaching for a fish. Nell jumped in. She couldn't find me.
Tam[happy]: I told Nell it wasn't her fault. She cried. Ghosts can cry, did you know? Then we laughed. We're going now.
guests.checkout: Tam[happy]: A river stone. It's warm if you hold it long enough.

guests.name: Bea
guests.bio: Sleeps with a nightlight. Ideally, a wisp in the room above.
guests.arrival:
Bea: Can I have a wisp upstairs? Like a nightlight? Or just someone next door.
No dark rooms. No screaming ladies.
story: Bea[sad]: Mum sent me to the country in the war. The hotel was the country. I didn't like the dark.
Bea: Ember sits upstairs and glows through the floorboards for me. I can see the cracks light up. It's nice.
Bea[happy]: I'm not scared of the dark now. I just like the light better. That's allowed. Bye!
guests.checkout: Bea[happy]: My torch. It only works for brave people.

guests.name: Aine
guests.bio: The eldest banshee. Enjoys noise. Likes corners.
guests.arrival:
Aine: I am Aine. I keened before your family had a name. Noise does not trouble me. I like it.
A corner, if there is one. Not a crowded floor.
story: Aine: Moira and Marisol keened each other free. I taught them, long ago. I am proud.
Aine[sad]: Vane bottled my sister's voice in 1801. It is on a shelf behind the cellar door. I can hear her.
Aine[happy]: Brigid uncorked the bottle. My sister sang her way out. Now I will follow her voice.
guests.checkout: Aine[happy]: An empty bottle. Never let him fill it again.

guests.name: Brigid
guests.bio: Aine's youngest sister. Hates the curse. Wants a corner, or solitude.
guests.hiddenHint: Little ones cry when they hear me. I can't bear it.
guests.arrival:
Brigid: Not a cursed room. Anything but. A corner, or alone.
And... please, be careful who you put beside me.
story: Brigid[sad]: I was the one Vane bottled. Aine says I've been out for a century. It doesn't feel like it.
Brigid: I'm going back in. Behind the door. There are other bottles. I know which corks are loose.
Brigid[happy]: Forty-one bottles. Forty-one voices. They're all singing on the way out. Listen!
guests.checkout: Brigid[happy]: A cork. The last one. Keep it, so nobody can use it.

guests.name: Una
guests.bio: A banshee who speaks only in riddles.
riddleClues: "Silence is my enemy. I sleep best where the house is loud."
"I keen above my sisters, never below. Or let the house be loud enough."
"The lake took my voice once. No water in my room."
guests.arrival: Una: (She only hums.)
story: Una: (She hums a tune. Bartholomew says it's one Edith used to hum.)
Una[happy]: (She hums the whole tune for the first time. Then she's gone, and the tune stays.)
guests.checkout: Una[happy]: (She leaves a tuning fork on the desk. It hums the same note.)

guests.name: Ember
guests.bio: A warm, steady wisp. Likes to watch over a knight, or a corner.
guests.arrival:
Ember: Ember. I glow, steady. Put me over a knight and I'll light their watch. Or a corner. I'm easy.
Not the cellar. Something down there eats light.
story: Ember: Lumen told me about the thing that eats light. It's real. It's Vane's warehouse, breathing.
Ember[sad]: I lit the knights' way to the door. Sir Corvin went through. He didn't come back yet.
Ember[happy]: Corvin came back. With jars. With lights in them. They're all going home. I'll light the way.
guests.checkout: Ember[happy]: A spark that never goes out. Keep it for the last night.

guests.name: Flicker
guests.bio: A nervous wisp. Upper floors only. Alone or with a friend, can't decide.
riddleClues: "Put me low and I'll go out. I live in the top two floors."
"I want to be alone. Or I want a friend. Either! Honestly, either."
"I make the dark rooms beside me less dark. Mind who sleeps there."
guests.arrival: Flicker: Hi! Top floors please! I'd like to be alone. Or not! Either! Sorry!
story: Flicker[sad]: I keep changing my mind because if I choose wrong, I might go out. That's what happened last time.
Flicker[happy]: I chose! I chose to go. It's fine. It's lovely, actually. Bye, bye, bye!
guests.checkout: Flicker[happy]: A match! Unstruck! For emergencies!

guests.name: The Hollow Squire
guests.bio: Sir Corvin's squire. Wants the lower floors, near his master or any company.
guests.hiddenHint: My master says never sleep where he has been.
guests.arrival: The Hollow Squire: (Just an empty suit of armour. It bows.) I serve Sir Corvin. Low floors. Near him, or near anyone.
story: The Hollow Squire: My body is in the warehouse. A jar on the third shelf. I can feel the cork.
The Hollow Squire[happy]: The cork is out. I am whole for one moment, and then I am free. Thank you, keeper.
guests.checkout: The Hollow Squire[happy]: My spurs. They jingle when someone's coming home.

guests.name: Sprocket
guests.bio: A clockmaker poltergeist. Lives in attics. Likes ticking company below or beside.
guests.arrival:
Sprocket[happy]: Sprocket! Clocks! The attic's where the clockwork is. Put a knight below me, they tick nicely.
Or anyone. No water, it rusts the gears.
story: Sprocket: Every clock in the hotel stops at 12:07. That's when Edith went through the door. I've been trying to restart them.
Sprocket[happy]: They're ticking! All of them! That means she's still in there. Still alive, in the way that counts.
guests.checkout: Sprocket[happy]: A spring. Wind it on the last night.
